Subject: Per-token tiers — we need an example of effective unit math for a phased commit

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the routing controls. Procurement asked me to get clarity on how Redwood's per-token tiering maps to an effective per-token price when we phase our commitment.

We expect a 12-month horizon but are fairly conservative for the first two quarters: a plausible ramp is 25M tokens q1, 80M q2, 220M q3, 400M q4 (total ~725M for year 1). Our legal team wants to understand: if we sign a 12-month commitment with quarterly true-ups, what does the invoice math look like under (A) marginal breakpoint pricing and (B) blended effective pricing?

I've attached our proposed commit schedule (acme_proposed_commit_schedule.xlsx). Can you produce 1) a short worked example that shows an invoice under both approaches and 2) any guardrails you need (minimum quarterly true-up, clawback windows, early-termination credit)?

Also, we have a procurement preference for smoothing so our unit economics don't jump between quarters — is that something Redwood can support (e.g., corridor smoothing or anchored breakpoints)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Cheers,
Olivia
Head of Cloud Integrations
ACME Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-token tiers — worked examples + phased options (draft)

Olivia — thanks for the schedule, and great to see the ramp profile. Attached is a short draft (redwood_phased-pricing-draft.pdf) with two worked examples and a recommended guardrail set. High level summary below.

Quick summary of options we put together:

1) Marginal ladder (classic breakpoints) — example pricing tiers (illustrative):
 - 0 - 100M tokens: $0.0009/token
 - 100M - 500M: $0.0006/token
 - 500M+: $0.00045/token

Under marginal math you pay the marginal rate on the tokens in each band. Example (using your annual projected 725M tokens):
 - First 100M at $0.0009 = $90,000
 - Next 400M at $0.0006 = $240,000
 - Remaining 225M at $0.00045 = $101,250
 - Annual spend = $431,250 => effective rate = $431,250 / 725M ≈ $0.000595/token

2) Blended (banded effective or "slab") — single effective rate applied to all tokens once you hit a breakpoint. If ACME structured as a slab with a 500M breakpoint and rate $0.0005 at that slab, the effective depends on which slab you finish the year in. For a 725M year the blended effective would be the slab rate for the highest achieved band (this can yield a lower invoice in months after the breakpoint, but has different cashflow implications).

Why smoothing matters:
 - With the marginal ladder you can see step-changes in invoiced unit cost as you cross bands, but invoices reflect usage precisely.
 - With blended/slab, once you hit the higher slab you get that flat per-token for all consumption (good for customer predictability once you hit a slab).

Recommended guardrails for a phased commit with quarterly true-ups (what we put in the draft):
 - Quarterly true-up window (7 business days after quarter close)
 - Corridor smoothing: allow a +/-20% corridor on the quarterly ramp vs committed profile without clawback for the first 2 quarters
 - Annual true-up + 60-day reconciliation window for catch-up credits or charges
 - Early termination: pro-rata true-up on committed discount uplift less a short termination fee (typical for reserved capacity deals)

I've included a worked monthly/quarterly invoice example on page 2 of the attached (two variants: marginal vs blended) using your numbers. If you'd like, Karthik can run a few alternate ramp scenarios (lower growth and a faster ramp) and we can table the one ACME prefers for the term sheet.

Happy to discuss on a call — available Wednesday afternoon.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Per-token tiers — worked examples + phased options (internal)

Ben — quick internal note before we finalize the draft for ACME. A couple of negotiation levers we could use:

1) Upfront credit in Q1 instead of a very aggressive first-breakpoint. For conservative ramps it's common to give a one-time $25k credit (applied in Q1) to help offset the effective $/token while they ramp.
2) Offer a "smoothing buffer" as you recommended but cap at 2 quarters — after Q2 we want the committed bands to be binding for pricing predictability.
3) If procurement pushes for blended/slab treatment across the year, we can offer a hybrid: apply blended pricing once they exceed 60% of annual committed volume by month 9, else fall back to marginal with a year-end true-up. That avoids premature slab escalations.

Karthik — can you confirm margin on the hybrid and the cashflow impact (one-line: expected ARR delta vs pure marginal) and whether legal is ok with the 60% trigger? If margin holds, I'll propose the hybrid + $25k Q1 credit as our concession.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the clear examples and the proposed guardrails. The worked numbers helped a lot. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

1) We prefer the hybrid approach you outlined (blended-on-threshold) if you can confirm the 60% by month 9 trigger and the $25k Q1 credit. Please convert that into a one-page term summary we can circulate in procurement.
2) Can you also add an invoice example that shows quarterly true-up math (we want to see how Q1 credit flows into Q2/Q3 invoices) and a sample early-termination calculation?

If you can get that to us by Friday EOD we can route to our legal and signers. We may have a short call Thursday to confirm a few numbers — how's 10am PT?

Appreciate the responsiveness — Olivia
Head of Cloud Integrations, ACME Health
